neighbours.label: text about a volatile or flammable substance giving off vapour (refrigerant, petrol fumes, solvents, a liquid turning to gas); fires on the words just before or around the vapour/gas mention, and its output promotes ' vapor', ' liquid', ' gas'. The - pole is the other side: inert airborne matter (air, coal dust, asbestos)
fire: The compressor raises the pressure of refrigerant before it enters the coil.
Never store petrol indoors because of the vapors it gives off.
Butane turns from a liquid into a gas as soon as the valve opens.
Acetone should be kept away from heat, since it is highly flammable.
The leaking kerosene evaporated and the fumes drifted through the workshop.
The varnish gave off a strong solvent smell and the windows were opened.
Ether boils at a low temperature and its vapour ignites easily.
The lighter fluid spilled on the bench and began to evaporate at once.
quiet: The pump raises the pressure of water before it enters the pipe.
Never store flour in damp rooms because of the mould it attracts.
Ice turns from a solid into a puddle as soon as the sun rises.
Sand should be kept near the forge, since it is highly useful.
The spilled gravel scattered and the dust drifted through the workshop.
The bread gave off a strong yeasty smell and the windows were opened.
Iron melts at a high temperature and its ore is mined nearby.
The milk spilled on the bench and began to drip onto the floor.

notes: Probes: refrigerant 0.82, solvent odour 0.81, flammable 0.66, vapors 0.63, liquid-to-gas 0.45, fuel fumes 0.43; coal dust 0.004, river water 0.002. Peak token varies ('ant', ' near', ' a', ' highly'), so this is a context, not a token.
